To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The employed shape model is capable of segmenting the liver in 3D CT scans with an average distance of 2.6mm and an average ratio of deviations larger than 5mm of 0.1.

the normalized gradient profile is the best appearance model for the segmentation of liver tumors, that the deformable model search is superior to the ASM search and that statistical shape modeling is very promising to segment the liver automatically.

the ASM search with a shape model based on 10 modes of variations and the deformable model search with a shape based on 30 modes of variations achieve the best results in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the segmentation of the liver in CT scans.
a fully automated segmentation method for the liver.
the development of a fully automated three-dimensional segmentation of the liver based on Active Shape Models (ASMs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ASM with 30 modes and a normalized gradient profile as appearance model achieves the best segmentation performance.
the ASM search with the normalized gradient profile and the deformable model coupled with the shape model deliver the most promising results.

the ASM search is a very promising technique for the fully automated 3D segmentation of the liver in CT scans, if the shape model is built with a large number of samples and if a normalized gradient profile is used as appearance model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of the normalized gradient profile with the ASM search using 30 modes achieves the best results in terms of accuracy and robustness.
statistical modeling of the gray-value appearance of the liver and the use of a deformable model with a shape model are essential ingredients for a successful liver segmentation.
statistical shape modeling is a very promising approach to segment organs with high variability in size and shape.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a shape model can be successfully built from a very small training sample and can be used to guide a deformable model to a good segmentation of the liver in clinical CT scans.
a statistical shape model is able to capture the shape variations of the liver and can be used for a fully automated 3D segmentation of the liver.
a shape model built with a small amount of training samples can be used to segment the liver from clinical CT data.
